data.one_liner: Physics-first Flutter animations with a composable, timeline-driven API
data.what_it_does: Provides a composable, timeline-driven API for physics-based and keyframed animations in Flutter without wiring imperative controllers through the widget tree. It separates triggers, actors, effects, and motions to create smooth transitions, state animations, and scroll-driven effects.
use_when: You want physics-based or spring animations without boilerplate animation controllers.
You need timeline-driven or scroll-driven UI motion in your Flutter app.
You want to organize complex UI animations into declarative actors, acts, and cues.
avoid_when: You are loading and rendering pre-compiled complex vector animations from external files (like Lottie).
You only need basic built-in implicit widgets and do not require timeline or physics configuration.
strengths: Clean separation between triggers, targets, effects, and motion curves.
Supports diverse trigger patterns including mounting, scrolling, hovering, and focusing.
Reduces controller boilerplate compared to standard AnimationController setups.
weaknesses: Requires learning a custom API and set of building blocks (Cues, Actors, Acts).
Actors throw an error if used without an ancestor Cue.

alternatives.name: flutter_animate
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer a simpler fluent extension-based API for quick chaining of widget animations.

alternatives.name: lottie
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you need to render complex designer-created vector animations exported from After Effects.

data.minimal_example:
Cue.onMount(
  motion: .smooth(),
  child: Actor(
    acts: [
      .fadeIn(),
      .slideY(from: 0.2),
      .scale(from: 0.96),
    ],
    child: const Text('Hello Cue'),
  ),
)
